about: The customer API contract as the verification tooling holds it: BUILD-SPEC section 6 of the Fable coding build (client contract customer-2026-11-26) - GET /api/session, GET /api/encounters and GET /api/encounters/<id> - every key listed and nothing else (studio/customer.py builds them; tests/test_api_customer.py holds the server to this file). Read by ops/scan_customer.py and the walk, so a key the server adds fails them until this file is consciously extended. Beyond section 6: workspace.specialty in GET /api/session (the workspace category's name - Gastroenterology, Neurosurgery or Orthopedic Surgery - a label the page shows; owner direction 2026-11-22, D390), document.view_media_type (what the in-page view shows: application/pdf, text/plain, or null when nothing can be shown) and document.converted (true when the view is the PDF a Word document was converted to for the coding review, so its pages are the pages the quotes name), and the state and phase 'earlier' (an encounter the earlier system reviewed, with no coding round: retry codes it again). The fix pass (FIX-SPEC section 1): every code row carries its line (L1.. the reader's codes in order, M1.. the second check's additions), and its decision, quotes and allowed_actions are that line's; modifiers are null when the coding review gave none (shown 'not given'); a question names the lines it affects (lines) and shows those lines' codes (codes). Fix pass 2 (FIX-SPEC-2 section 5): a decision shown carries its id, which an undo (POST decisions, action revoke) names as decision, and an export (POST reports) names the round the page shows; either is answered 409 when it no longer matches. The physician PDF report (2026-11-21): an export is made as pdf only (studio.exports.FORMATS; owner direction 2026-11-21, no more TXT or CSV); a listed export made before that may be csv or txt, so the fmt enum keeps all three. Types: string, integer, number, boolean, any, date (YYYY-MM-DD), iso (an ISO 8601 timestamp); a trailing '?' allows null. A node is a type name, {"ref": NAME, "nullable": bool}, {"enum": [...], "nullable": bool}, {"items": NODE}, {"map": NODE} (any key, values of NODE) or {"keys": {...}, "nullable": bool} (exactly these keys). Release 1 (the build of 2026-11-24; RELEASE-1-SPEC C4 and C5): GET /api/session adds can_manage_team (true for an active owner: owners only see and change the team, owner decision D15); GET /api/members answers members (a practice's memberships, each a member: id, label, username, role, active - their access to this practice, the switch an owner turns - actor_kind, last_sign_in and password_change_required; username is a key the customer denylist forbids elsewhere, so a reader of this payload exempts it); POST /api/members/<id>/access {active: true|false} answers member_access ({member}); a refusal there is the usual {error, details} (403 for a reviewer or viewer, 404 for someone of another practice, 409 for your own access or the last active owner). Over a report, upload or bundle limit any API call answers 429 rate_limited ({error: rate_limited, retry_after: whole seconds}, with the same number in the Retry-After header): the page says it in its own words. Release 2 (the build of 2026-11-26, client contract customer-2026-11-26; RELEASE-2-SPEC R2-19 to R2-21, R2-16 and R2-24): GET /api/encounters serves one page of a list - ?list=documents (no list means documents), queue or recent, and ?before=<cursor> for a later page - as list: encounters (Documents and the Review queue 50 rows a page, the Overview's recent 5), newest first (created_at, then id); next, the cursor of the next page (a UTC time to the microsecond and an id, `<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.ffffffZ>~<id>`), or null when nothing follows (always null for recent); and total, the list's exact number (for the queue, of the documents waiting on a member) on a first page, null for recent, a later page and a search; and workspace, the id of the practice the page was read in (the member's active practice at that request: after the member's access changes, a later page or a search may be another practice's, which the page never draws - it reads the list afresh; integrated refutation round 1, exact-0). POST /api/encounters/search {text, before} (CSRF; the words only in the body, never in an address) answers the same list shape over every document of the practice whose row, as the page draws it, holds the words (total null); a blank text is answered 400, a text longer than 240 characters or holding a character the database cannot store an empty page. An unknown list or an unreadable cursor is answered 400 {error, details}; a later page or a search over the member's limit 429 rate_limited. Each list_row adds opens_pdf: true when the document's first stored file is a PDF of at most 1 MiB, so the page may ask for its view at the click. The in-page view (GET /api/encounters/<id>/original?view=1, outside the contract) of a stored PDF carries ETag, a quoted UUID derived with a key from the sign-in, the document and the stored file's hash - never a hash itself - and answers 304 with no body to If-None-Match naming it (recorded as a read, shown from the page's memory). The page shell carries GET /api/session's payload in <body data-session-json>. Integrated refutation round 1 (viewer-0): document.view_round names the coding round whose conversion a Word document's view serves (the newest round that stored one, none once a later round refused the file), null for every other document and for a Word document with no view: a later round that converts the file again (C8) serves another PDF at the same view_url, and the page redraws its viewer whole when view_round changes.
